transcript: Hi, so, a disagreement with a colleague. Um, okay. There was a time a colleague in sales and I both thought a lead was ours. It was a company that came in through the website, but I had also met their director at an event a month before, so I felt it was my lead. She said the website leads were assigned to her that month. We were both a bit upset about it and it went to our manager. The manager decided we would share it, so we both went to the meetings. It was a bit awkward in the beginning, honestly, because the client didn't know who to talk to. In the end we closed the deal and split the commission. It was fair in the end. What I learned is that we should have a clear rule for who owns a lead, because it wastes time when two people argue. After that the team made a rule that the first person to log it in the CRM owns it, and that helped. Sorry, I can explain this better, I might record it again.
